## Reference Commit: `b48037b` — `2dust/v2rayN`

**What it does:** Adds `Utils.GetPunycode(url)` in [`v2rayN/Tool/Utils.cs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/2dust-v2rayN/-/blob/v2rayN/v2rayN/Tool/Utils.cs) and calls it in [`Handler/UpdateHandle.cs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/2dust-v2rayN/-/blob/v2rayN/v2rayN/Handler/UpdateHandle.cs) before issuing an HTTP download of a subscription URL. The utility parses the URL with `System.Uri`, compares `uri.Host` to `uri.IdnHost`, and if they differ, replaces the non-ASCII hostname with its Punycode equivalent. Falls back silently on any exception.

**Eligibility axes to match:**
| Axis | Target value |
|---|---|
| Language | C# |
| Framework/API | `System.Uri`, `uri.Host` / `uri.IdnHost`, .NET |
| Engineering intent | IDN-to-Punycode normalization of a URL string before network use |
| Stratum gate | Code must pre-date cutoff `cf8dd45abe3dd54667a3ce0e6923695acbf10823` |
| Change size | Small: ~25 lines, 1 new utility method + 1 call site |
| Exclusions | Vendored, generated, tutorial, fixture, copied |

## Candidate 1 — `dotnet/aspnetcore` (v9.0.0 mirror)

**Repository:** [`github.com/sg-evals/aspnetcore--v9.0.0`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/aspnetcore--v9.0.0)
**File:** [`src/Middleware/CORS/src/Infrastructure/CorsPolicyBuilder.cs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/aspnetcore--v9.0.0/-/blob/src/Middleware/CORS/src/Infrastructure/CorsPolicyBuilder.cs?L67-90)

**Implementation:**

```csharp
internal static string GetNormalizedOrigin(string origin)
{
    ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(origin);

    if (Uri.TryCreate(origin, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) &&
        (uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttp || uri.Scheme == Uri.UriSchemeHttps) &&
        !string.Equals(uri.IdnHost, uri.Host, StringComparison.Ordinal))
    {
        var builder = new UriBuilder(uri.Scheme.ToLowerInvariant(), uri.IdnHost.ToLowerInvariant());
        if (!uri.IsDefaultPort)
        {
            builder.Port = uri.Port;
        }
        return builder.Uri.GetComponents(UriComponents.SchemeAndServer, UriFormat.Unescaped);
    }

    return origin.ToLowerInvariant();
}
```

**Eligibility check:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Language: C# | **Pass** — `.cs` file in a .NET project |
| API: `System.Uri`, `uri.IdnHost`, `uri.Host` | **Pass** — identical .NET BCL types used; same `Host == IdnHost` guard to detect IDN hostnames |
| Engineering intent | **Pass** — converts an IDN host in a URL string to its Punycode form before storing it; functionally equivalent normalization step |
| Change size | **Pass** — `GetNormalizedOrigin` is a focused ~20-line static utility method with a single call site (`WithOrigins`), matching the scope |
| Not vendored/generated/tutorial | **Pass** — live production middleware code inside the ASP.NET Core framework |
| Stratum / cutoff | **Pass** — `aspnetcore--v9.0.0` is a pinned release mirror; the CORS Punycode normalization was introduced in ASP.NET Core well before the v2rayN cutoff SHA in 2022; the feature is documented as existing in .NET 6+ CORS middleware |
| Not a copy of v2rayN | **Pass** — independent codebase, different domain (CORS origin allowlist vs. subscription URL download), different method structure (`UriBuilder` reconstruction vs. `string.Replace`), different null handling |

**Notable structural divergence:** `aspnetcore` reconstructs the full URL via `UriBuilder` to also normalize scheme casing and strip default ports; v2rayN does a simpler `url.Replace(uri.Host, uri.IdnHost)`. Both compare `uri.Host` to `uri.IdnHost` as the detection mechanism and return the input unchanged when already ASCII. The unit test file [`CorsPolicyBuilderTests.cs`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/aspnetcore--v9.0.0/-/blob/src/Middleware/CORS/test/UnitTests/CorsPolicyBuilderTests.cs?L412-425) explicitly exercises Punycode conversion with IDN inputs (e.g., `http://Bücher.example` → `http://xn--bcher-kva.example`), confirming the intent is identical.

Because this is the same upstream source file at a different snapshot, it should be treated as a single logical match with two study-corpus entries rather than two independent implementations.

## Non-candidate: `gitlab-org/gitlab` — `lib/banzai/filter/external_link_filter.rb`

This Ruby file contains `punycode_autolink_node!` and `idn?` helpers that detect IDN hostnames and expose Punycode in link tooltips. **Excluded** for the following reasons:

- **Language mismatch:** Ruby, not C#
- **Framework mismatch:** uses `Addressable::URI` / `uri.normalize`, not `System.Uri`
- **Engineering intent is adjacent but distinct:** the purpose is malicious-link UI disclosure (adding a tooltip), not transparent URL normalization before a network call
- **No analog to `uri.IdnHost` comparison** — uses `uri.normalized_host.start_with?('xn--')` as the IDN test, a heuristic rather than a platform-provided IDN comparison

---

| **2 (same source, alt pin)** | `sg-evals/aspnetcore--87525573` | `CorsPolicyBuilder.cs` L67–90 | Same as above; second study-corpus entry of the same upstream implementation |
| ~~gitlab-org/gitlab~~ | ~~`external_link_filter.rb`~~ | — | Excluded: wrong language, different intent |
